results.summary_before: This 8-bit ALU loads two operands into internal registers A and B from an 8-bit data bus and executes arithmetic, logic and shift operations selected by a 3-bit opcode. Control signals on the bidirectional pins trigger loading and execution, and the result appears on the 8-bit output with zero and carry flags. The documentation gives a worked example of adding 7 and 5, and no external hardware is required beyond switches and LEDs on a demo board. It is a simple teaching-oriented design with no silicon test results reported.

results.summary_before: This analog circuit provides a zero-temperature-coefficient (ZTAT) voltage reference, designed to be stable across temperature variations. It is tested by measuring the VREF pin at different temperatures, with the rate of change expected to be within 1.2 mV. External hardware includes a high-precision multimeter and an environmental chamber or thermal stream. The design is a simple bandgap reference, notable for its low temperature drift.

results.summary_before: This design is a pre-trained Binary Neural Network (BNN) for 8x8 MNIST digit classification, implemented in SystemVerilog. It serially loads a 64-bit image and outputs a 4-bit prediction (0-9) after processing, with a reported test accuracy of 70%. The network consists of 18 neurons and is combinational for minimal area, requiring no external hardware for operation. The project is notable for being a silicon-hardened neural network accelerator on a Tiny Tapeout tile, albeit with reduced accuracy due to area constraints.

results.summary_before: This project implements a simple interdigitated metal-oxide-metal capacitor that fills a 1x2 analog tile. It provides two active terminals and two dummy terminals for parasitic control, with an estimated capacitance of around 85 pF from magic extraction. The capacitor is intended for measurement using test equipment such as a function generator and oscilloscope or a VNA. The design is a passive test structure with no active circuitry.

results.summary_before: This design is an FSM-driven dot product engine that reads input data on ui_in, controls a small register/memory bank, and performs multiply-accumulate operations. Control bits select idle, work, or debug modes, and status flags plus a debug selector expose internal state and results on the bidirectional and output pins. It is verified with a cocotb testbench that checks reset, state transitions, status changes, output values, and debug readback. No external hardware is required, and the project is presented as a learning-oriented Tiny Tapeout implementation.
